about: A security scanner that finds known holes in the software packages a project or container uses.

prs.title: npm workspaces with similar names no longer add a fake package
prs.broken: With two workspaces like "packages/ui" and "packages/ui-kit", Trivy could file one under the other. Which one won changed from run to run, and some runs listed an extra package with no version.
prs.changed: A workspace now only claims its own folder and the folders inside it, not any folder whose name starts the same way.
prs.matters: Scans of npm workspaces give the same, correct package list every time.

prs.title: Yarn packages keep their real names and are no longer dropped
prs.broken: Trivy read settings nested deep inside a yarn.lock entry as if they were the entry itself. Some packages showed up under another package's name, and others were dropped with an error.
prs.changed: Trivy now reads a package's name, version and dependencies only from the lines where Yarn puts them, and skips the nested settings.
prs.matters: Yarn projects get scanned under the right package names, so known holes are matched to the right packages.
